stem: Ritu writes the prime factorisations $168=2\times2\times2\times3\times7$ and $12=2\times2\times3$.

parts.text: Which claim about divisibility is correct?

options.text: $168$ is divisible by $12$ because both factorisations include the prime $2$.
$168$ is divisible by $12$ because $2\times2\times3$ from $12$ is included in the factorisation of $168$.
$168$ is not divisible by $12$ because $168$ has prime factors that $12$ does not have.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A number is divisible by another when every prime factor of the divisor, with enough repeats, appears in the first number. Here $2\times2\times3$ sits inside $168$'s factorisation.

teacher.key_rationale: Enough copies of each prime of 12 appear in 168, so 168 is divisible by 12. Sharing only the prime 2 omits the full factor condition. Extra primes in 168 do not block divisibility and reverse the inclusion test.
